sentences.text: Hello and welcome to the Slow English Podcast.
My name is Emuly.
I'm happy you are here today.
In this episode, we will talk about Iraq.
Iraq is a country in the Middle East
with a long and rich history.
Let's learn about Iraq in slow and simple English.
Are you ready?
Let's begin.
Where is Iraq?
Iraq is in Western Asia in the Middle East.
It is next to Turkey, Iran, Syria,
Jordan, Kuwait, and Saudi Arabia.
Iraq has a short coastline on the Persian Gulf.
The country has deserts, rivers, cities, and mountains.
What is the capital city of Iraq?
The capital city is Baghdad.
Baghdad is a large and busy city.
It is located near the Tigris River.
Baghdad is one of the oldest cities in the world.
It was a center of science, learning, and culture in the past.
Today it has schools, markets, mosques, and government buildings.
How many people live in Iraq?
About 44 million people live in Iraq.
Most people live in cities like Baghdad, Basra,
Mosul, Erbil, and Najaf.
Some people live in villages or in the mountains in the north.
Iraq is a country with many different cultures and languages.
What language do people speak in Iraq?
The main language is Arabic.
Many people also speak Kurdish, especially in the north.
Some people speak Turkmen, Aramaic, and Assyrian.
In schools and universities, people also study English.
What is the weather like in Iraq?
Iraq has a hot and dry climate.
Summers are very hot, sometimes more than 45 degrees Celsius.
Winter's are mild and sometimes rainy.
In the north, it can even snow in the mountains.
There are two big rivers in Iraq, the Tigris and the Euphrates.
They bring water to farms and cities.
What does Iraq look like?
Iraq has different landscapes.
Deserts in the west and south, mountains in the north,
green areas near the rivers, cities with history and modern life.
In the north, the Kurdistan region has hills, forests, and cool weather.
In the south, there are marshes, wetlands with reeds and water buffalo.
What animals live in Iraq?
Iraq has many animals, especially in the countryside.
You can see sheep, goats, camels, and donkeys.
In the marshes, you can find buffalo, fish, and birds.
In the deserts, there are foxes, snakes, and lizards.
Cows, chickens, and horses also live on farms across the country.
What do people eat in Iraq?
Iraqi food is warm, rich, and full of flavor.
People eat rice with meat or vegetables, lamb, chicken, and fish.
Flatbread, called cubs.
Dates, Iraq is famous for dates.
Lentil soup, beans, and grilled meat.
Popular dishes include doma, vegetables stuffed with rice and meat.
Kibob, grilled meat on skewers.
Mascoof, grilled fish, especially in Baghdad.
Cuba, fried or baked dough with meat inside.
For dessert, people eat baklava, halva, and sweet rice pudding.
What do people drink in Iraq?
People drink tea many times a day.
It is strong and sweet, often with sugar.
Coffee is also common, especially in the north.
People also drink water, juice, and sometimes yogurt drinks.
What is life like in Iraq?
Life in Iraq can be different in each region.
In the cities, people go to work, school, and markets.
In the villages, people grow food, care for animals, and live in close families.
Family is very important in Iraq.
People often live with parents, grandparents, and children together.
People enjoy music, cooking, storytelling, and visiting each other.
Evening tea is a special time to sit, relax, and talk.
What are some holidays in Iraq?
People in Iraq celebrate many holidays.
Some are religious, and some are national.
Eid al-Fetor, at the end of Ramadan.
Eid al-Ada, the Feast of Sacrifice.
Neuraz, Kurdish New Year, celebrated in March.
Iraqi Independence Day, October 3, Ashura, important for many Muslims.
On holidays, people wear nice clothes, visit family, and share food.
Some fun facts about Iraq.
Iraq is part of the ancient land called Mesopotamia.
It is known as the Cradle of Civilization.
The first writing, the wheel, and early laws came from this area.
The flag of Iraq is red, white, and black, with green writing.
The Tigris and Euphrates rivers were home to ancient cities like Babylon and Ur.
The national dish of Iraq is Ma's goof, grilled river fish.
Now you know many things about Iraq.
You know where it is, what people speak, and how they live.
You learned about the food, culture, weather, and traditions.
Great job!
I am Emili.
Goodbye.
Or as they say in Arabic, Ma Salama.
